rv.q: The test of any La bohème is whether it brings a tear to your eye. This one did.
All of this was channeled by the acute awareness of conductor Ramón Tebar and this proved to be a most historical "La Bohème" to behold.
Here was where De Tommaso’s mastery of nuance and Grigoryan’s dialing her voice from inmost pianissimo to full-throated longing made the text come palpably to life.

cn.t: Critics praise this Met production, with Freddie De Tommaso earning particular acclaim for heroically stepping in as Rodolfo while also performing in Macbeth. Strong performances across the cast impress reviewers.
